description: Improve the first-minute mining loop by guaranteeing visible, reachable low-tier ore near the starting shaft.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh to serve and observe the current game before editing.
Inspect src/world.ts, src/constants.ts, src/balance.ts, and the existing world/state tests to understand deterministic ore generation and starting-position constraints.

Adjust early-depth world generation so a new player can find and mine several Coal/Copper ore tiles within roughly the first 40-80 m around the starting area without making deeper ore progression trivial.
Keep the change deterministic and DOM-free; avoid hard-coding a brittle single route if a small starter seam or early-depth density rule is clearer.
Add or update unit tests that verify near-start early ore availability while preserving late-game special tiles, hazards, enemies, and the Motherlode core behavior.
Run ./init.sh and perform a live smoke where the intro is dismissed and the player mines enough early tiles to collect at least one ore item.
acceptance: In a fresh live browser run, the player can reach and collect at least one low-tier ore within the first short descent from the surface without wandering blindly for multiple screens.
The top of the mine still contains dirt/air navigation decisions and does not become an all-ore tutorial corridor.
Automated tests cover deterministic early ore availability and guard against regressing the existing world-generation landmarks and hazards.
Before marking complete, run ./test.sh plus canonical verification npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build.

description: Show clearer cargo value and next-upgrade feedback during early mining runs.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh and observe the HUD/cargo flow before editing.
Inspect src/ui.tsx, src/game.ts, src/economy.ts, src/dom.ts, and the UI/startup tests to locate HUD hooks and existing cargoValue/cargo-detail behavior.

Add a compact always-visible or easily discoverable HUD readout for current cargo value and/or the amount needed for the cheapest affordable next upgrade so mining rewards are understandable without opening the info dialog repeatedly.
Update the readout after mining, selling, buying upgrades, save/load, reset, and empty/full cargo transitions without breaking existing DOM IDs/classes consumed by the game runtime.
Add or update tests for the new HUD hooks and any DOM-free formatting/helper logic used to compute cargo value or upgrade guidance.
Run ./init.sh and perform a live smoke that mines/sells or manipulates cargo enough to see the new feedback change.
acceptance: During play, the HUD or info surface clearly communicates current cargo value and useful next-upgrade affordability/progress feedback.
The feedback updates correctly after cargo changes, selling, upgrades, save/load, and reset flows.
Existing HUD meters, alert flashing, controls, and React startup behavior remain intact.
Before marking complete, run ./test.sh plus canonical verification npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build.
